dispositionReason: The implementer's own disclosed residual gap (getOperativeProvision never sets ToolExecutionOutcome.evidenceUnresolved) is REAL and, contrary to the implementer's own explicit claim in docs/phase-3f1-final-closure/04-evidence-trust-context-fix.json's residualRisk[0] ('FIX-2's context-bundle-level and defense-in-depth gates independently cover the same underlying scenario... so this residual gap does not currently permit VERIFIED/COMPLETED'), THIS CLAIM IS FALSE for a section that (a) is genuinely OPERATIVE_STATE_CONFLICTED, (b) is reached ONLY via a real getOperativeProvision tool call, and (c) is never itself embedded in the context bundle (not the candidate's own primary operative source, not auto-discovered as a cross-reference/definition-dependency). A fresh, independently-constructed end-to-end reproduction (real StructuralIndex/OperativeContractState/CovenantContextBundle/RealSemanticCaller tool-use loop/compileCovenantToIR/verifyCompiledCandidate/persistSemanticTruthForInstrument, real Postgres) demonstrates the compilation reaches status COMPLETED, verification reaches a VERIFIED_* status, and the persisted SemanticTruthRecord.trustStatus is VERIFIED (appearing in getTrustedSemanticTruth) - off a rule whose only real justification came from a section two independent, competing amendments left with no single legitimate current text.

claimTestedDirectly.implementerClaim: "this residual gap does not currently permit VERIFIED/COMPLETED off a CONFLICTED section reached via THIS tool alone reaching a materially different rule than the one already covered" (04-evidence-trust-context-fix.json, residualRisk[0])
claimTestedDirectly.verdict: FALSE as a general claim. It happens to be true ONLY in the narrow case the implementer's own test file actually exercises (test group 2 of part-a-final-fix2-context-trust.test.ts), where the CONFLICTED section IS the candidate's own primary operative source - in that specific case the section is independently caught by unrelated pre-existing mechanisms (the context bundle's own OPERATIVE_SOURCE item, sourceInventory.supersessionStatus, and compilerInput.operativeLineage, all of which are keyed off the candidate's own sourceSectionRef). None of those three independent mechanisms apply when the CONFLICTED section is a DIFFERENT section from the candidate's own source and was never independently embedded in the context bundle - the exact shape this recertification constructed and confirmed unsafe.
claimTestedDirectly.rootCauseOfTheGap: compile.ts's OPERATIVE_STATE_UNRESOLVED gate ORs exactly three signals: (1) toolCallLog[].evidenceUnresolved - never set true by getOperativeProvision regardless of the section's real status; (2) contextBundle.hasUnresolvedOperativeEvidence - only reflects items the context-retrieval pipeline itself embedded, never an arbitrary section fetched later via a tool call; (3) hasStaleReferencedDefinition - scoped ONLY to IRDefinition.termName, never to a SECTION a rule's own capacityExpression may have been informed by. verify.ts mirrors the identical three-signal gap (hasUnresolvedDefinitionEvidence/hasUnresolvedContextBundleEvidence/hasStaleReferencedDefinition), plus its own sourceInventory.supersessionStatus/operativeLineage checks, which are ALSO scoped only to compilerInput.sourceSectionRef (the candidate's own primary section), never to a section reached only via a tool call.

Turn 2: submit_compilation with one rule (sourceSectionRef 6.01, capacityExpression $5,000,000, sufficiency COMPLETE) - the model disregards the CONFLICTED status the tool's own response disclosed to it.
